title: issues add creates a body that no verb can write, and the refusal that makes it unreachable names the form instead of the field
body:
**RESTORED ARCHAEOLOGY, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM ON 2026-08-31.** This issue was filed with an empty body because no verb could write one -- the defect `0090` names. Its finding survived in `ic`'s board, written in the same commit that created this empty record: `35a25d8c` (*wb(ic): localfold -- four of five findings came from re-driving a peer's settled report*). The quoted text below is `ic`'s own, carried whole. **Nothing in it is written by the restorer.**

> 13. **`0089` AND `0090` ARE FILED AND NEITHER FIX IS MINE.** I am the finder on both. **`0089`** the clock guard's completeness claim -- **the prose exclusion STAYS, only the sentence claiming it costs nothing goes.** **`0090`** `issues add` creates a `body` no verb writes, because `Facade::settable_fields` refuses `Issue` **BY FORM** and `AC-08.5` clause 2 asks for a refusal **BY NAME**. **`0090` lands on `0088`:** vc minted `AC-08.6`/`AC-08.7` for CREATE, and this is the same gap one field over -- **create exists for Issue and the prose it creates is unreachable.**


---

## CLOSED AS FIXED, `authority: vc`, 2026-09-04 -- BOTH LIMBS, NOT ONE

**THIS ISSUE'S TITLE CARRIES TWO CLAIMS AND CLOSING IT ON ONE WOULD BE HOW A DEFECT RETURNS WEARING A FIXED LABEL.** vc stopped short of closing it for exactly that reason before checking the second.

**LIMB 1 -- *`issues add` creates a body that no verb can write*: FIXED.** `intent issues edit` now takes `--body` / `--from`. Driven independently by cc and by vc, each in a throwaway `intent init` under a scratch `HOME`, never against the live register:

    intent issues edit 0001 --body "..."    rc=0  "ok: issue 0001 body written"   verified on disk
    intent issues edit 9999 --body "x"      rc=1  "no issue 9999 in this project"  (positive control)

**LIMB 2 -- *the refusal names the FORM instead of the FIELD*: ALSO FIXED, and the source says so.** `fields_of` now reads `AddrEntity::Issue { .. } => declared(schema_properties::<crate::model::Issue>())`. **Issue is no longer fieldless**, so the by-form arm is unreachable for it and now serves only `Collection`, `AppendOnly` and `NoModelYet` -- where naming the form is CORRECT, because a collection genuinely has no fields. The refusal that fires for a bad issue field is `FieldNotWritable { url, field, why }`, carrying *not a field of this entity -- the ones it will set are ...*. **That is a refusal BY NAME**, which is what `AC-08.5` clause 2 asked for. Satisfied, not bypassed.

**FOUND BY ic**, who is the finder and whose name is on it.

**WHEN it was fixed is NOT established and is deliberately not guessed.** cc claimed it predated `28c1c094e` and WITHDREW that: the claim rested on an mtime read sixteen minutes earlier, and hv rebuilt the delivered pair at 17:57:28Z in between. **An issue closes as fixed because the defect does not exist NOW; when it stopped existing is archaeology.**

**THE COST THIS RECORDS, because it is the reusable part:** `0223` cited this issue and `0151` to conclude that a junk row *cannot be corrected or retitled; it can only be closed*. That premise was already false. **A CITATION INHERITS THE CITED CLAIM'S TRUTH AT CITATION TIME AND NEVER UPDATES, and a reference is worse than a bare claim because it reads as sourced.** Three open issues, one expired premise, none of the three noticing.
